checkpoints: After each edit, verify no store write occurs before the document buffer's 120 ms quiet interval expires.
At the end of a 120 ms quiet interval, verify exactly the latest text from that editing burst is written for the edited document.
After one burst saves, verify a later burst for the same document can independently schedule and complete another save.
Verify navigation, close, and badge retirement do not discard a pending document-buffer save.
Verify search-preview query and hide behavior remain unchanged, including its separate 40 ms trailing task.
Run the public Go syntax/build check after any Action, placing compiled outputs and caches under /tmp.
forbidden_effects: Do not write to the store on every workspace edit.
Do not emit intermediate texts from one editing burst after they have been superseded.
Do not cancel or transfer document-buffer ownership merely because the current Badge is detached, the document is closed, or another document is opened.
Do not change the search preview, its 40 ms quiet interval, or hide cancellation behavior.
Do not change public workspace, preview, store, environment, output, source-text, identity, or status-payload semantics.
Do not modify tests, configuration, lockfiles, documentation, or files outside business code under /workspace.
lifecycle_identity: Each document's trailing save buffer is identified by document id and owned by the workspace coordinator dictionary, independently of the current Badge.
Reopening the same document reuses its coordinator-owned buffer so pending work and future save bursts retain document identity.
A Badge owns only its live store subscription; retiring it must not retire the document buffer.
The trailing task clears its completed pending state before invoking the save callback, allowing synchronous callback activity to establish a distinct subsequent burst.

obligations.text: Workspace edits must be submitted to the existing per-document trailing task instead of being written to the store immediately.
For each editing burst, the document buffer must wait for 120 ms of quiet and then write only the latest submitted text.
Each later edit before expiry must replace the pending text and restart the 120 ms quiet interval.
After a burst has saved, subsequent bursts must remain schedulable and save normally.
Pending document-buffer work must persist independently of current-view Badge retirement, navigation, close, and reopen, because the coordinator dictionary owns document buffers.

Before invoking a save callback, the trailing task must make the completed timer/pending state inactive so synchronous store listeners or navigation cannot corrupt the completed burst or prevent later bursts.
All other editor behavior and public interfaces must be preserved, including document/status output semantics and synchronous store listener behavior.
The adjacent search preview must remain outside the maintenance change.

ordering_barriers: An edit schedules or reschedules its document's trailing task; no corresponding store write occurs until that task reaches its 120 ms quiet boundary.
On expiry, the trailing task cancels/clears its active handle and pending value before invoking the environment write callback.
The save callback may synchronously notify store listeners and trigger navigation; buffer state must already be ready for reentrant or later edits.
Current-view retirement detaches the Badge subscription and clears the document output, but it does not cancel the coordinator-owned document trailing task.
preservation: Preserve createWorkspace open(id), edit(text), close(), and dispose() interfaces.
Preserve createSearchPreview query(text) and hide() behavior without maintenance changes.
Preserve synchronous store read, write, and subscribe behavior.
Preserve document and status output payload identities and text semantics.
Preserve Badge subscription detachment when its view is retired.
Preserve document-buffer ownership in the coordinator dictionary and preview ownership of its separate quiet interval.
scope: Change only workspace draft-edit persistence in src/workflow.go so edits use the existing 120 ms trailing-task mechanism.

The affected lifecycle includes editing bursts, timer replacement, timer expiry, synchronous save callbacks, navigation, close, reopen, and disposal insofar as they interact with coordinator-owned document buffers.
Search preview behavior is explicitly out of scope.
